entities.name: Battle of the Persian Gate on the Mountain
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of the Persian Gate on the Mountain, fought in 329 BCE, was a pivotal event in the ancient world, pitting the Macedonian army of Alexander the Great against the Persian forces of Ariobarzanes in a treacherous mountain pass known as the Persian Gate. This decisive clash marked a turning point in Alexander's conquest of the Achaemenid Empire, as he successfully broke through the Persian defenses and opened the door to further conquests in the ancient Near East. The aftermath of the battle saw the fall of Persepolis, the capital of the Achaemenid Empire, and the integration of the Persian Empire into the vast Macedonian dominion.

The battle itself was a testament to Alexander's military genius, as he employed innovative tactics to counter the Persian forces, including the use of phalanx formations and clever deployment of his cavalry. The Persian army, led by Ariobarzanes, was ultimately unable to withstand the might of the Macedonian forces, and the outcome of the battle was all but certain.

In the years that followed, the Battle of the Persian Gate on the Mountain had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of ancient history and leaving an indelible mark on the world.

As the ancient Greek historian Arrian noted, 'The battle was a turning point in the conquest of Asia, and it showed that the Persians were not invincible.'
